title: Xen grant-copy cache validation flaws permit cross-domain arbitrary memory read and write
organization: Anthropic and Xen Project; validated by Ada Logics; independently reported by CodeAnt AI Security Research Team
summary: Incorrect revalidation of cached grant-copy details can mix frame numbers and grant references (CVE-2026-102703), or place the check restricting frame-number copies to caller-owned memory incorrectly (CVE-2026-102704). Xen’s primary advisory says a malicious guest can read and write arbitrary memory belonging to other domains, including Dom0. The two CVEs are separately identified manifestations in one XSA-523 underlying grant-copy cache-validation issue, so this record counts the shared discovery once.
ai_role: The signed primary Xen advisory explicitly says the issue was discovered by Anthropic using Claude, then validated by Stephan Lipp of Ada Logics; it also notes an independent report by CodeAnt AI Security Research Team.
classification_note: XSA-523 was publicly released Nov 3, 2026. The advisory explicitly separates the two CVE manifestations but presents them as one grant-copy validation issue; they are grouped here as one distinct discovery. No exploitation-in-the-wild claim is made.
remediation_note: Apply the appropriate attached XSA-523 patches to the relevant Xen stable branch. The advisory lists no known mitigation. Deployment status is not checked.
